players.product: ZeroFlap AECs, optical DSPs (Robin/Cardinal), SiPho PICs (Dust Photonics), retimers for AI clusters

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026 record results: revenue of $407 million, up 52% sequentially and more than tripling year-over-year, at the high end of the revised guidance range; non-GAAP gross margin 68.6% (above the high end of guidance, up 92 basis points sequentially); non-GAAP operating margin 49.6%; non-GAAP net income a record $208.8 million, quadrupled from Q3 of last year. Record operating cash flow of $166.2 million; CapEx of $26.5 million driven largely by purchases of production mask sets; free cash flow $139.7 million; cash and equivalents of $1.3 billion after the ATM offering that ran from October to December. CEO Bill Brennan: revenue more than doubled from fiscal '24 to fiscal '25 and Credo expects to triple it in fiscal '26 - 'greater than 6x growth in just 2 years'.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue of $407 million, up 52% sequentially; non-GAAP gross margin of 68.6%; non-GAAP net income $208.8 million; cash flow from operations $166.2 million; CapEx $26.5 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2026 guidance and first fiscal 2027 outlook (CFO Dan Fleming): Q4 revenue between $425 million and $435 million; non-GAAP gross margin 64% to 66% (a conservative forecast - the long-term model stays at 63% to 65%); non-GAAP operating expenses $76 million to $80 million; diluted share count approximately 197 million, based on the current tariff regime, which remains fluid. For fiscal '27 Credo expects sequential revenue growth in the mid-single digits, leading to more than 50% year-over-year growth. Fleming: fiscal '26 ends 'just north of $1.3 billion' and 'The 50% growth gets you to nearly $2 billion for next year', with ZeroFlap Optics expected to be a material component of fiscal '27.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue between $425 million and $435 million; gross margin 64% to 66%; fiscal '27 more than 50% year-over-year growth; nearly $2 billion for next year

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration: growth came across 4 domestic hyperscale customers, and the top 3 end customers were each greater than 10% of revenue and all grew sequentially. Largest customer 39% of revenue (also the largest in Q1 - a large quarter-to-quarter increase); second largest 32% (the largest customer last quarter); third 17% (the first hyperscaler Credo ramped). Credo expects 3 to 4 customers above 10% in coming quarters; the fourth hyperscaler, while in line with expectations, may not be a 10% customer for the full year because of upside from the largest customer. Credo is diversifying across hyperscalers, Neoclouds and other customers.
quarterly_data.figure: largest customer 39%, second 32%, third 17% of revenue; 3 to 4 customers greater than 10%

quarterly_data.signal: AECs grew again, driven by existing customers and new wins INCLUDING A FIFTH HYPERSCALER, with demand accelerating at hyperscalers and emerging Neocloud providers. Brennan: AECs are now the de facto standard for intra-rack and rack-to-rack connectivity up to 7 meters, increasingly displacing laser-based optical modules; ZeroFlap AECs deliver up to 1,000x better reliability than commodity laser-based optics at roughly half the power. Large-scale deployments run at 100 gig per lane with a long tail; 1.6-terabit AECs will support Ethernet, UALink and ESUN, and PCIe Gen6 AECs are sampling now for mass production in first half fiscal '27. At 200 gig per lane the value proposition is stronger with an ASP uplift, though reach shrinks 'from 7 meters to 5 meters'. Credo's strength is scale-out (with front end coming along; a couple of customers deploying in switch racks / disaggregated chassis); front end is expected to be 20% to 25% of the scale-out market. Brennan on 200G: 'NVIDIA is going to lead the charge with Vera Rubin, but many other customers will follow on a slower time line', and that market will be addressed by AECs plus laser-based modules, with ALCs ramping in.
quarterly_data.figure: fifth hyperscaler; up to 1,000x better reliability at roughly half the power; up to 7 meters (from 7 meters to 5 meters at 200G); PCIe Gen6 AECs mass production first half fiscal '27

quarterly_data.signal: ZeroFlap Optics PULLED IN: progress is ahead of schedule - production shipments began with the first Neocloud customer, Tensor Wave (joint announcement covering both AECs and ZF Optics), and 3 additional customers including hyperscalers and Neocloud operators are in qualification. Last quarter Credo signaled a second-half fiscal '27 ramp; it now expects a significant production ramp beginning in the first quarter of fiscal '27 and continuing through the year - 'we pulled in 6 months', driven by customer pull. Brennan: 'We've got 4 in now' and expects more than 4 customers ramping during fiscal '27. ZF Optics adds continuous link-flap telemetry and autonomous mitigation via the Pilot software with switch-level SDK integration - the first time an optical transceiver has been taken up the stack to deliver real-time telemetry - and lets Credo address optical connectivity at any length inside the data center.
quarterly_data.figure: ramp pulled in 6 months to the first quarter of fiscal '27; 4 in now, more than 4 expected; 3 additional customers in qualification

quarterly_data.signal: IC business (optical DSPs and retimers across 50G/100G/200G per lane): strong optical DSP growth expected in fiscal '26 on 100 gig per lane deployments, with increasing 200 gig traction as customers prepare for 1.6T transitions and 'a lot of uplift right now for LRO' as power becomes more important at 200 gig. Ethernet retimers growing significantly at 100 gig per lane in switching fabrics and AI servers; PCIe Gen6 retimer design wins in fiscal '26 expected to convert to production revenue in fiscal '27. Blue Heron, a 200 gig per lane retimer for scale-up supporting UALink, ESUN and Ethernet, announced its first customer, upscale AI, and Credo will build AECs with it. Brennan: 'We don't have any revenue for scale up' today - the bulk of AI revenue is scale-out. There will be an ASP uplift from 800 gig to 1.6T across the entire portfolio.

Three new multibillion-dollar TAM expansions: (1) Active LED cables (ALCs), built on micro LED expertise from the Hyperloom acquisition, bring AEC-class reliability, power and cost to mid-reach optical with a thinner gauge cable - reach initially up to 10 meters, then up to 30 meters; sample and qualify in fiscal '27, production ramp in fiscal '28. (2) OmniConnect gearboxes pair Credo's VSR SerDes with gearboxes for XPU connectivity: the first product, Weaver, enables up to a 10x improvement in memory beachfront I/O density at reach up to 10 inches by converting VSR to DDR; first customer Pozitron plans an inference XPU with 2 terabytes of memory capacity; first gearbox production ramp in fiscal '28, with future gearboxes for LPDDR6, PCIe Gen7/Gen6 scale-up and 200G/400G per lane making XPUs composable. (3) ZeroFlap Optics. Brennan positions Weaver as relief for the memory crunch by enabling DDR over HBM, 'probably the tightest area within the memory market right now'.
quarterly_data.figure: ALC reach up to 10 meters then 30 meters, production ramp fiscal '28; Weaver up to a 10x improvement in memory beachfront I/O density, up to 10 inches; 2 terabytes of memory capacity

quarterly_data.signal: CPO view: Brennan says CPO noise is dominating the signal - 'it's not an either/or type of situation' - and the industry is moving to a heterogeneous mix of short-reach copper, pluggable optics, near package optics and eventually CPO. Until NPO and CPO can deliver bulletproof reliability deployments will be somewhat limited, 'which is why many of the forecasters show low single-digit share in the switching market over the next 3 years'; for the 200G per lane generation, 'CPO is still sometime in the future beyond that'. Credo plans an OmniConnect gearbox converting VSR to micro LED (proven out by the ALC work) as a lower-risk path to a near package optics solution at much lower power than laser-based CPO.
quarterly_data.figure: forecasters show low single-digit CPO share in the switching market over the next 3 years

quarterly_data.signal: Supply position: Brennan feels great about supply for all product categories - wafers at 12-nanometer, 7, 5 and 3 - after aligning with supply chain partners at both wafer and packaging level last quarter, enough to support the plan plus expected upside; no system-level supply issues. On industry laser concerns, Credo has 'more than underpinned our demand for '27 and really beyond' for ZF Optics after two years of underpinning supply and firm commitments to supply chain partners. Q3 ending inventory was $208 million, up $57.8 million sequentially. Brennan: supply chain 'is going to become more and more of a differentiator'.

Credo announced and closed the Chimera acquisition on the day of the call. Chimera had been a Credo IP partner since 2022 with a strong reputation in protocol IP, error correction and security IP; its team will be dedicated to Credo projects to accelerate the end-to-end connectivity road map, including moving up into higher-layer solutions. Q3 non-GAAP operating expenses of $77.4 million were up 35% sequentially on a large R&D step-up (project-related spend and hiring).
quarterly_data.figure: non-GAAP operating expenses $77.4 million, up 35% sequentially
